page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.se1.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. The Intel Xeon processor delivers weak single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1100.49 and a multi-core score of 2931.93. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block operations recording a poor 20.19 GB/sec and write operations at 18.14 GB/sec. Computational tasks such as bzip3 decompression and gzip compression fall into the bottom 10% of tested systems.

Given the high memory allocation relative to compute resources, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. It is suitable for caching layers, lightweight database operations, and memory-bound applications. However, the poor database operations score of 1073.82 and weak Redis SET performance of 2.87 million operations per second indicate that high-throughput transactional databases may face performance bottlenecks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for memory-heavy, compute-light workloads where raw processing speed is secondary to memory capacity.
